A1.justification: Despite retitling and substantial revision, both PDFs share the GNN scoping problem, core subgroup-generalization analysis and AS visualization. Their main texts and appendices support comparison; rendered pages resolve extraction difficulties with tables, figures and equations.

before.justification: V2 reports original node-classification experiments, accuracy/ROC-AUC results, runtime comparisons, ablations and embedding visualizations in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 reports original Moscat and Moscat* benchmark results, comparison experiments, ablations, case studies and extensive supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: V2's AS predicts a scope ID and selects one expert, using KL divergence and Gumbel-Softmax. V3 instead combines per-expert augmented representations through attention and an MLP classifier trained on node labels with cross-entropy. It also introduces heterophily-biased sample filtering. Independently trained depth variants remain, and AS survives as an appendix visualization variant.

E1.justification: V3 adds ogbn-arxiv to the reported node-classification evaluations. Flickr was already evaluated in v2 Figure 2, while Chameleon and PubMed remain represented in v3's appendices despite leaving the main comparison table. The overall task and most graph coverage remain stable.

E2.justification: V3 Table 2 adds evaluated Graph Transformer and Graph MoE comparisons, including GraphGPS, SGFormer, GMoE, Mowst and DA-MoE; Polynormer expands from a leaderboard entry to this comparison. Table 3 adds residual/initial-residual/self-concatenation controls but drops v2's GAT scoping-comparison block. Table 9 adds GNN-ft and GNN-mlp controls.

E3.justification: For eta=0.1, gate training changes from 10% of validation data in v2 Equation 11 to 90% in v3 Appendix F.2. Moscat* adds training-only holdouts, complementary splits and output averaging. New studies vary expert dropout, width and training epochs. The Penn94 leaderboard configuration also changes from SAGE-AS with maximum depth 6 to MixHop-Moscat with maximum depth 16.

E4.justification: V3 replaces AS's separate feature/split ablations with holdout, multi-scope, heterophily-filtering and logit-augmentation tests. It adds validation-data controls, expert-training sensitivity studies, prediction-overlap matrices, gating-weight diagnostics and the genius case study. Existing oracle and depth analyses are expanded; the AS t-SNE visualization is retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions state ten runs and report plus/minus values. V3 explicitly identifies the uncertainty measure as standard deviation in checklist item 7, reports uncertainty in its ablation table and specifies different random seeds for the fixed-depth oracle control. These changes do not establish an increased run count.

E6.justification: Moscat/Moscat* results replace AS results under changed methods and splits, alongside extensive new comparison and diagnostic results. Retained comparator entries also change: H2GCN on amazon-ratings is 36.47±0.23 in v2 Table 1 and 46.31±0.44 in v3 Table 2. Leaderboard entries and rankings change too; cross-version method scores should not be interpreted as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The CSBM/SGC assumptions and principal lemma/proof largely carry over. V3 adds a risk decomposition, broadens the definition of personalized scoping and revises the displayed bound and its properties. A localized inconsistency appears: its main-text coefficient is E[(p-q)^(L-1)], whereas v2 and the retained v3 appendix derivation use (E[p-q])^(L-1).

C1.justification: V2 centers its contribution on formalizing personalized scope-size classification and solving it with AS. V3 centers a decoupled expert-gating paradigm for improving deeper GNNs with shallow variants. Its principal performance claim expands to comparisons against Graph Transformers and Graph MoEs, beyond the earlier GNN-focused claims.

C2.justification: V3 expands the overfitting explanation into representation, optimization and generalization tradeoffs. It adds explanations for heterophily-biased filtering, recovering useful information from incorrect expert predictions, architecture-dependent training sensitivity and learned gating weights. It also newly states possible ineffectiveness on highly homophilous graphs, exemplified by homophily above 0.8.

D1.justification: V3 announces a code repository, newly documents software versions and CPU/GPU hardware, and provides complementary-split parameters and revised gating configuration tables. Runtime reporting additionally includes expert-plus-gate time under a parallel-training assumption, rather than only the added gate cost. However, v2's explicit 60%/20%/20% PubMed split disclosure is lost despite retaining PubMed results.

R1.justification: Much of the earlier personalized-scoping discussion moves to Appendix A, but positioning substantively expands around deeper-GNN failures and Graph MoEs. V3 adds relevant depth/generalization literature, a Graph MoE subsection and discussion contrasting its training strategy with jointly trained LLM MoEs and ensembles. Newly cited works include GMoE, DA-MoE, GraphGPS, SGFormer and PathMLP.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution narrative and method exposition are extensively rewritten around Moscat and the depth dilemma. Related work and substantial preliminaries move to appendices, and the supplementary material is reorganized into a much more detailed analysis structure with a conference checklist.

P2.justification: The document changes from an ACM two-column layout to a single-column preprint layout. V3 adds paradigm and workflow diagrams, restructures comparison tables, and introduces extensive heatmaps, sensitivity tables and diagnostic plots. Existing figures are also redistributed, including the AS t-SNE visualization, which becomes Figure 12.

improvement.justification: Moscat* and the matched validation-data controls in Appendix F.2/Table 9 address an important untested label-budget confound in v2. New MoE comparisons, component ablations and expert-training studies substantially strengthen empirical support, while code and environment disclosures improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, including the new main-text/proof coefficient inconsistency and lost PubMed split disclosure, which still limit theoretical precision and reproducibility.
